reuse.why: The change reuses tag extraction, month utilities, spreadsheet access, budget writes, batching, and undo wrappers while sharing category exclusions across all month-wide consumers.

duplication.why: Shared SQL conditions remove repeated category filtering, although the new action repeats the income eligibility guard already present in each existing action.

placement.why: Category selection and budget calculations remain in the server budget actions module, with method registration in the existing app layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, focused tests, and a release note.

maintainability.why: The shared exclusion definition makes future policy changes straightforward, although its implicit SQL aliases and parameter contract introduce some coupling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All affected month-wide actions use getMonthWideCategoryConditions through getBudgetData or getMonthWideCategories and retain existing budget mutation abstractions.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated income guard is explicit, and the category exclusion logic is shared rather than reshaped into separate implementations.

abstraction_drift.where: The shared selection helpers gain includeHiddenCategories, with one conditional in getMonthWideCategoryConditions selecting hidden-category filtering; every affected consumer uses that definition.
